Sec. 6801 directs a GAO review of AARO's implementation of 50 U.S.C. 3373; sec. 6802 sunsets the GAO audit requirements attached to the Historical Record Report. Wiring it here fixes a degree-1 orphan and records the first enacted step in winding oversight machinery back down rather than up.

edges.label: P.L. 119-60, Title XVI Subtitle E - the enacted corpus reduced to housekeeping
edges.note: Approved 18 December 2025, with three UAP sections requiring that AARO briefings cover NORAD and NORTHCOM intercepts and accounting for UAP classification guides. Recording it in the enacted domain alongside the 2021-2023 provisions is what lets a reader see the trajectory of what Congress has actually been willing to enact.

edges.label: the largest operator of the one acquisition form built to be non-competitive by design
edges.note: MITRE operates multiple FFRDCs. FAR 35.017 permits an agency to meet special long-term research needs through a sponsoring agreement with a single operator outside full and open competition, and obliges the FFRDC to disclose its activities to its sponsor and to no one else. That is a contracting mechanism, and MITRE is its largest single instance.

edges.label: the prime where classified contract line items and sworn allegation meet
edges.note: Lockheed Martin's prime contract obligations run to the hundreds of billions of dollars in USAspending records, a portion carried as classified line items visible in financial systems only as a number. It is also the only company named on the floor of a congressional hearing by a sworn witness in connection with the custody allegation, which makes it the test case for whether contracting records can be made to answer the question.

edges.label: sensor-side prime - the contractor-generated data category nobody is asking for
edges.note: Raytheon builds the AN/APG-79 and ATFLIR families through which the military detects and images the objects at issue, which makes it the corporate custodian of a withheld category of contractor-generated sensor data distinct from the custody allegation. Graded Tier 2: no source places Raytheon in any UAP-specific contract vehicle, and the edge rests on documented prime-contractor role plus hearing-record discussion of sensor data.

edges.label: contracting at a site whose existence was itself classified
edges.note: EG&G instrumented and fired US nuclear tests from the Manhattan Project onward and became the classified services contractor for the Nevada complex, including the Air Force operating location near Groom Lake - a facility whose existence required a Presidential Determination published at 60 FR 52823 to exempt it from disclosure. It is the historical template for how contracting works where the place of performance cannot be named.

edges.label: a company stood up to hold a single government contract
edges.note: BAASS was registered as a legal entity distinct from Bigelow Aerospace, with its own DUNS and CAGE codes, in order to bid and hold DIA contract HHM402-08-C-0072. Standing up a corporate vehicle for the purpose of receiving one award is a contracting mechanic, and it is the one instance on this board that is fully documented in FOIA-released procurement paper.

The DIA transmittal list to SASC and the published list of funded studies establish the subcontract layer, which is the layer at which visibility normally stops.

edges.label: a non-FAR instrument binding the Army to a private claimant of recovered material
edges.note: Signed 10 October 2019 by the Director of the Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center and announced 17 October 2019. A Cooperative Research and Development Agreement sits outside ordinary procurement, involves no exchange of appropriated funds to the partner, and protects the private party's proprietary data - which is exactly the class of vehicle this domain is about. The executed document is not public; sourcing is the partner's own contemporaneous FAQ.

edges.label: the FFRDC seam is a species of contracting mechanics, not a separate subject
edges.note: FAR 35.017 is a procurement regulation. The records status, disclosure direction and sole-source features that make the FFRDC form load-bearing on this board are all properties of the contracting instrument, which is why the seam domain should hang off contracting mechanics rather than float beside it.

recommend_collapse.reason: Collapse. d-money's own description begins by saying it 'narrows d-funding to a single question' - a domain defined as a narrowing of another domain is a facet of it, not a peer. The membership sets do not separate cleanly: the classified annex, MIP, NIP, waived USAPs and 10 U.S.C. 119 all satisfy both tests, and the disjoint split written into this file (audit and opacity to d-money, named channels to d-funding) is an editorial choice that could be reversed without loss, which is the diagnostic for a distinction without a difference. Keep d-funding because 'Funding Channels' states a membership test a node either passes or fails (is this a route money travels?), whereas 'Black Budget & Unaccounted Funds' states a conclusion, and the board's tier discipline prefers testable membership to argued membership. On collapse, fold the DoD audit-disclaimer material into d-funding's description as its unaccounted-funds facet and re-point the existing d-funding -> d-money edge, which becomes self-referential.

Do NOT collapse d-legislative into d-legislation. The membership sets produced in this pass are fully disjoint: d-legislative holds S.Amdt. 797, the UAPDA of 2023, the FY2027 House-adopted amendment, the SSCI committee provision, and the four institutional actors that move text; d-legislation holds only enacted law - 10 U.S.C. 119 and the FY2022, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 acts. Nothing appears in both. Proposal versus enactment is also the board's central substantive finding (the Review Board and eminent domain provisions passed the Senate and were stripped in conference), so merging the two would erase the thing the board is arguing. 'keep' is set to d-legislation only to name the id that would survive if a collapse were forced against this recommendation; the recommendation itself is to keep both. Suggested improvement short of collapse: relabel d-legislative to 'Legislative Process (proposed and pending)' so the boundary is legible from the node label alone.

Not one of the pairs asked about, but found during this pass and worth raising: dod-sapco and dod-sapco-arch carry the identical label 'DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)' and identical descriptive content drawn from the same two issuances, DoDD 5205.07 and DoDI 5205.11. They are one institution entered twice. Keep dod-sapco (degree 11) and re-point dod-sapco-arch's 6 edges onto it. Only dod-sapco was wired to d-structure in this file so that the collapse does not have to be undone afterwards.

unresolved: iaa-fy2024-sec-1102 carries a section number that does not match any text I could verify. The contractor turn-in provision with the 60-day notification and 180-day availability deadlines is Section 1104 of S. 2103 as reported by the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, not Section 1102 (Section 1102 of that bill concerns notification on the provision of defense sensitive support). The node id and label should be corrected. An existing board edge, iaa-2024 -> iaa-fy2024-sec-1102, already carries the annotation 'section number needs verification'; this pass confirms the annotation was warranted.

Whether the contractor turn-in requirement survived into enacted law is unresolved. The enacted counterpart is Sec. 7343 of Division G of P.L. 118-31, 'Funding limitations relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena.' The Senate Select Committee's own Joint Explanatory Statement describes 7343 as imposing a funding limitation and an independent-research-and-development indirect-expense limitation, and does not describe a turn-in duty; the contemporaneous Mirador analysis records that the enacted UAP provisions 'differed substantially' from what Senate committees and the full Senate had approved. I could not retrieve the operative text of Sec. 7343 from a primary source: govinfo's PLAW-118publ31 HTML and the Senate Intelligence Committee's Division G page both served only front matter and the section list on fetch, not the section bodies. Because of that, iaa-fy2024-sec-1102 was wired to d-legislative and d-funding at Tier 2 and deliberately NOT to d-legislation. Resolving this needs the govinfo PDF page range for Division G Subtitle C.

d-structure -> manhattan-project-2 is Tier 3 and rests entirely on two UAP Gerb YouTube videos (1 May and 19 June 2026). No independent documentary corroboration exists for the onion model as a description of an actual architecture. It is wired because the domain is about structural argument and this is the argument, not because the architecture is established.

raytheon -> d-contracting is Tier 2. No source places Raytheon in any UAP-specific contract vehicle, programme or SAP. The edge rests on its documented role as the prime for the ATFLIR and AN/APG-79 sensor families plus general prime-contract volume in USAspending. If a stricter standard is applied this edge should be the first cut.

the-hill -> d-media is Tier 2. The sourced record shows coverage and opinion placement aimed at a congressional readership; I found no original documentary investigation by The Hill in this subject area, so the edge label says placement rather than investigation.

ttsa-army-crada: the executed CRADA instrument itself is not public. Sourcing is To The Stars Academy's own archived FAQ from 2019 and 2021. The signing date, the signatories and the named points of contact all come from the partner rather than from the Army, and no FOIA release of the agreement has surfaced.

waived-sap-notification-group carried no sources at all on the board before this pass. The two edges written here source it to 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2), which is the provision that creates the channel. The composition of the group as eight members - chair and ranking member of each of the four defense committees - follows from the statutory text; any narrower 'Gang of Eight' framing found elsewhere on the board should be checked against it.

aawsap-contract-hhm402-08-c-0072 and iaa-2024 each appear in two of my domains (contracting and funding; enacted statute and funding). Both are deliberate and the notes state which fact carries which membership, but if the d-money/d-funding collapse is accepted these should be re-checked for redundancy.
